http/message#

Requests and responses: a head (method, target, status, fields, version) and a body.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let request = Request(url: "https://example.com/", headers: Headers(Header(name: "Accept", value: "text/html")));
request::Head::method;                                   // Method.get
request::Head::target.path();                            // "/"
let body = await request.text(limit: 65536);

Description#

Requests and responses: a head (method, target, status, fields, version) and a body.

A request is its head and its body, made apart and put together:

let head = RequestHead(
    method: Method.post,
    url: "https://api.example.com/orders",
    headers: Headers(Header(name: HeaderName("Accept"), value: "application/json")),
);
Request(head: head, content: JsonBody(order));       // a Content
Request(head: head, body: opening);                  // any BodyOpening, unread
Request(url: "https://api.example.com/orders", method: Method.post, content: JsonBody(order));

A RequestHead is the method, the target, the fields and the version, checked to fit; the request keeps it as its only copy of them, and Request::Head shows it. A request made from a Content gets the content's media type as Content-Type unless its fields name a compatible one (the same type and subtype, carrying the content's parameters; ConflictingContentType otherwise), and its length as Content-Length when the body knows it and the fields frame it neither by Content-Length nor by Transfer-Encoding. A body of unknown length gets no length: the client frames it for its protocol. A request made from a BodyOpening keeps its fields as given. Making a request reads, opens and closes nothing. Query parameters belong to the URL (UrlParts.query_appended), credentials to the client (http/auth).

Response(status: Status.ok, content: TextBody(text: "hi"));
Response(status: Status.no_content);

Unless told, a request is a GET with no fields, an empty body and HTTP/1.1; a response has no fields, an empty body and HTTP/1.1. A message never reads its body itself: the connection or the handler does. A Responding is anything that builds a Response, such as the replies in web/reply.

Request.bytes#

async bytes(limit is int) is @byte

The whole body, at most limit bytes: await request.bytes(limit: 65536). A longer body throws BodyLimitExceeded, without being read when it declares its length (#76). A body in memory is handed out as it is; a streamed one is copied once, when its chunks are joined.

async text(limit is int) is string

The whole body as UTF-8 text, at most limit bytes.

object Response#

object Response does Responding

A response shows its head through the cap Head; body() is the opening to read. Unless told, it has no fields, an empty body and HTTP/1.1. Like a request it is its head and its body, made apart and put together:

let head = ResponseHead(status: Status.created, headers: location);
Response(head: head, content: JsonBody(order));     // a Content
Response(head: head, body: opening);                // any BodyOpening, unread

From a Content it takes the content's media type as Content-Type unless its fields name a compatible one (ConflictingContentType otherwise) and the known length as Content-Length unless its fields frame the body, as a request does; from a BodyOpening it keeps its fields as given.

Errors#

  • BodyLimitExceeded: a body read whole was longer than the limit.
  • InvalidHttpMessage: a head that does not fit together.
  • ConflictingContentType: fields name a Content-Type the content contradicts.
